name: Torsten Pröfrock
editorial_article:
Torsten Pröfrock is a German electronic musician and sound engineer deeply associated with the Berlin techno scene, particularly the seminal dub techno label Chain Reaction. Emerging in the 1990s, he built a reputation for a precise, texture-heavy approach to electronic production, operating under a dense web of aliases including T++, Dynamo, Erosion, and Traktor. His work is characterized by an obsessive attention to microscopic sonic detail, blending the deep, hypnotic pulses of dub techno with intricate, often syncopated rhythmic structures.

Pröfrock gained significant prominence as a collaborator with Robert Henke in the project Monolake, where his technical influence helped shape the project's signature crystalline, spatial sound design. Beyond his group contributions, his solo output—most notably under the T++ moniker—pushed the boundaries of what was considered 'dub' or 'techno,' often experimenting with complex polyrhythms and stark, cavernous environments. Throughout his career, he has remained a pivotal, albeit somewhat enigmatic, figure in the evolution of minimalist electronic music, influencing a generation of producers interested in the intersection of dub experimentation and modern digital synthesis. His work serves as a masterclass in the digital interpretation of traditional dub studio aesthetics.
